title: Contract Coherency Graph compilation and supported logical coherency
statement: Every governed repository MUST compile its canonical Module Contract v2, recursive containment, selected standard logic, and supported verification declarations into one deterministic provenance-preserving Contract Coherency Graph whose currently supported obligations are logically coherent.
rationale: One derived semantic IR lets every evaluator consume the same dependency, constraint, guarantee, Feature, and verification meaning while distributed contracts remain the sole authored intent authority.
failure_prevented: Ambiguous providers, stale dependency intent, incompatible versions, duplicate identities, invalid proof targets, broken inheritance, dependency cycles, conflicting effective rules, incomplete provenance, and competing contract-resolution models.
applicability: Every governed repository using Fortress Module Contract v2.
evaluation: Fortress compiles the ecosystem once, derives containment, inverse consumers, dependency and capability reachability, inherited and implied constraint closure, guarantee and Testing support topology, preserves behavior declarations, verifies provenance integrity and deterministic serialization, rejects supported contradictions, and compares contract-derived outbound relationships with README projections.

finding.message: CCG compilation failed or a currently supported semantic obligation is incoherent.

remediation: Correct the precise source contract, capability, relationship, rule implication/conflict, effective constraint, guarantee, Feature, requirement, verification declaration, provenance, or README projection identified by the CCG finding.
valid_example: A consumer requires one compatible capability from its exact provider; the CCG derives its dependency, inverse consumer, reachability, and provenance without treating the capability as re-exported.
invalid_example: A Module's effective rule closure contains two formally conflicting rules or its capability dependency closure contains a directed cycle.
exception_policy: Implemented compilation and logical gates have no local exemption. Arbitrary natural-language contradiction, general behavioral satisfiability, source dependency realization, security information flow, runtime-consumer ownership inference, and general theorem proving remain explicitly unsupported rather than passing.
history: Introduced with Module Contract v2 as the first deterministic ecosystem intent resolution rule.
Upgraded by CCG v1 to govern one provenance-preserving semantic IR and its supported logical coherency closure.
